version.changelog:
- Initial release of aux-mcp: "Spotify for your AI" with DJ, party, roast, and auto-DJ features via MCP integration.
- Supports mood-based music selection, playlist roasting, weekly reports, party rooms, and dynamic DJ features through user queries.
- Provides setup instructions for both CLI and OpenClaw integration.
- Requires Spotify Premium for playback; browsing and searching work with just client credentials.
- Includes guidance for preferred tool use, error handling, and displaying interactive ASCII cards from tool responses.

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent Spotify integration, but it asks users to run an unpinned npm package that handles Spotify credentials and tokens, so users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's credential use is purpose-aligned, but the unpinned package is given `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` and `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` and participates in OAuth/token handling under `~/.aux-mcp/`, which is high-impact without version pinning or integrity guidance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The setup and MCP registration use unpinned npm/npx execution for `spotify-aux`, including `npx -y spotify-aux`, so the executable code can change after review and runs with the user's local privileges.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most runtime instructions are Spotify-specific, but some activation phrases such as "Keep it going" are broad enough that the agent could invoke Spotify actions outside clearly music-related context.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill documents local token storage, global npm installation, OpenClaw MCP registration, and copying the skill into managed skills; these are disclosed and purpose-related, but they persist beyond a single interaction.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities fit the stated purpose: Spotify playback, recommendations, playlist analysis, party queues, and local helper commands through an MCP server.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the `spotify-aux` npm package and publisher. Prefer a pinned, reviewed package version before running login or MCP registration, and understand that the package will receive Spotify app credentials, manage local OAuth tokens, register an MCP server, and may run local helper services for AutoDJ or party hosting.
llm.findings:
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted as a material review concern: multiple artifact instructions run `spotify-aux` through unpinned npm/npx, including login, MCP server startup, helper modes, and local skill installation.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the artifact depends on mutable third-party package execution while also passing Spotify credentials and handling local OAuth state.
[AS3] expected: Downgraded: the cited text says the helper copies its own `skills/aux-mcp/SKILL.md` into the user's OpenClaw skills directory, not that it enumerates or reads unrelated installed skills.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partially accepted as a scope-quality note: broad trigger phrases could cause over-invocation, but this is not the main security driver for the verdict.
